headline: Bitcoin is holding near $64,500 after a weekend drop below $62,000, with fear at extreme levels as traders wait for Fed Chair Warsh at noon ET and the biggest options bet now on a fall below $60,000.

market.asOf: Read at about 15:57-15:59 UTC Mon 16 Nov (about 23:00 Bangkok) from CoinGecko's pages. The 24-hour change is left out because sources disagree: CoinGecko's bitcoin page showed down 1.60% while CoinMarketCap's homepage showed up 2.02%. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear, read at about 15:58 UTC: Alternative.me's index 10 (Extreme Fear, 13 yesterday), CoinMarketCap's index 12, CoinGecko's own index 21 (27 yesterday). They are different indexes, so the numbers do not match.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $64,500 after a weekend drop below $62,000; the biggest options bet is now on a fall
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $62,000 over the weekend, its lowest in about four months, bounced to about $65,500 after the US stock market opened and later traded near $64,500. It has now lost ground six weeks in a row. On the options market, where traders pay for the right to buy or sell later at a set price, the single biggest bet is now protection against bitcoin falling below $60,000.
points: The weekend low was $61,950 on Bitstamp, a four-month low, per Cointelegraph; Coinbase's low was $61,998.26, per The Crypto Basic.
Bitcoin rose to about $65,500 after the US open, per CoinDesk's live coverage at 9:39am ET, which calls this its sixth weekly loss.
Bitcoin is down 17% in November per CoinDesk's live coverage, 16% per CoinDesk's Daybook.
Open interest, the total value of open futures bets, fell 9.1% to $20.98B from Friday to 10:00 UTC Monday, per CryptoQuant data cited by Cointelegraph.
The largest bitcoin option position on Deribit is the $60,000 put (a bet on a fall), about $900M, ahead of the $100,000 call at about $867M, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Rates week: Warsh speaks at noon ET, a December hike is priced in, and the 10-year yield is above 5%
stories.summary: Fed Chair Warsh gives opening remarks at a San Francisco Fed conference at noon ET today; he had not spoken when this was written. Futures traders see a December interest-rate rise as close to certain; that is a market bet, not a Fed decision. Higher rates and bond yields pull money away from risky assets like crypto, and US spot bitcoin ETFs have had seven straight days of withdrawals.
points: CME FedWatch odds for a December hike are put at 92% for a 0.25-point rise and 8% for 0.5 points by KuCoin, and at 100% by the Motley Fool using data as of 12 November.
The US 10-year Treasury yield was 5.116%, versus 4.83% a week ago, and the Nasdaq was down about 2% in the first hour of trading, per CoinDesk's live coverage.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $185.4M on Friday 13 November, their seventh straight day of outflows, about $1.91B in total, per Farside data cited by CryptoTicker.
Fed minutes from the October meeting are due Wednesday at 2pm ET, and US retail sales Tuesday, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Strategy buys only 485 bitcoin as most of its stock sale goes to buying back preferred shares
stories.summary: Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, kept buying last week but in a small amount. Its filing shows most of the money it raised by selling its own shares went to buying back its preferred stock, not to bitcoin. Its average cost per bitcoin is now above the market price.
points: Strategy bought 485 BTC for $33.4M, at an average $68,887, between 9 and 15 November, per its SEC filing.
It now holds 850,849 BTC bought for $64.20B in total, an average of $75,452 per coin, per the filing.
It sold 2,087,040 of its own shares for $244.7M; $206.3M went to buying back STRC preferred stock, per the filing. CoinDesk puts that buyback at $228.1M.
Strategy's shares were down 8.3% before the US market opened, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Binance hack recovery and the Arbitrum vote
briefs.summary: Binance says withdrawals are back on 87 networks and aims to restore the rest by the end of next week after the $6.3B hack, per Investing.com; an Arbitrum DAO vote on returning 8,425.997 ETH and 74.56M ARB of frozen funds ends 16 November, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: US moves to seize $1.2B tied to the Binance hack
briefs.summary: The Justice Department got court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2B linked to the hack and says more than $2.7B has been frozen in total, per NewsBTC.

briefs.title: Bitcoin miners hijacked at Luxor
briefs.summary: Attackers redirected mining power from just over a dozen customer accounts and collected about 0.243 BTC; Luxor patched the hole within 2 hours and will reimburse customers, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: OKX and Binance founders trade blame
briefs.summary: OKX's Star Xu blamed Binance for crashes; CZ denied Binance sold and said he bought; Binance co-founder Yi He disclosed a $97.3M trading loss, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Solana ETFs see six weeks of outflows
briefs.summary: SOL hit a weekend low of $67.41 and US Solana ETFs have had six straight weekly outflows totalling $197.4M, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Bitmine keeps adding ether
briefs.summary: Bitmine bought 7,653 ETH (about $15M), taking its holdings to about 6.07M ETH, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Upbit owner swings to a loss; XRP treasury firm writes down
briefs.summary: Dunamu posted a Q3 net loss of 18.6B won and Evernorth recorded $271M of impairments on its XRP over nine months, per Analytics Insight.

briefs.title: Russia opens crypto to ordinary investors
briefs.summary: From 17 November non-qualified retail investors in Russia can buy BTC, ETH and USDT up to an annual cap, per CoinDesk.
